title: America Is A Reflection Of Ancient Assyria | Part 1

sense.text: Christ read this in Luke 4, and after he read it, they tried to throw him off a cliff. “To preach good tidings unto the meek”: that’s what we’re doing, preaching good tidings to the men and women who humble themselves to the word of Almighty God. “To bind up the brokenhearted”: that was Christ’s job, and that is our job. “To proclaim liberty to the captives”: when you read this Bible you read about the children of Israel in slavery, from one captivity to the next to the next, and here we are today under the United States of America, some of us under Europe and other countries. We are a captive people. “And the opening of the prison to them that are bound”: we are bound in prisons.

“And the day of vengeance of our God”: the churches never talk about the day of vengeance of our God. That day is soon approaching. “To comfort all that mourn”: we are mourning because we are in captivity, colonized, enslaved; we are brokenhearted.

“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion”: he’s going to appoint to us that mourn in Zion. “To give unto them beauty for ashes”: that’s a heavy statement. The first thought is God is going to give us a kingdom, but I’m going to scratch the surface before we get to the kingdom. If he’s going to give us beauty, what is the opposite of beauty? Ugly. We have been taught to hate the way we look: our hair, our complexion, the size of our nose, our lips, everything about us. The movie Farming is a true story about a Nigerian actor who, between the 1960s and 1980s, was farmed out to a white family in England while his parents finished school. They broke this brother’s spirit; he hated himself and he hated all black people, and he had to be re-taught how to love himself. The captain who watched it with me added that there are layers of self-hatred we have to penetrate on the streets before our people can even come to the sense that they are Israel. Another brother told of a young sister in Sierra Leone who was taught scripture after scripture that Christ is black and could not accept it; she cried, threw the flyer on the floor and ran, because in her mind black is no good and only white is good. So we got a big job to do.

Isaiah is prophesying about the Assyrian captivity that was about to take place. There were three campaigns against Israel; the last one they attempted was against the kingdom of Judah, because Israel had already been split by this time. “Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees”: they made unjust laws regarding our people. The Assyrian empire had unjust laws, just like America: the 13th Amendment has a clause that allows re-enslavement of people convicted of a crime, and Tim Wise admits his own family took advantage of the headright program, which gave European men 50 acres of land, and the Homestead Act of 1862 gave out 240 million acres to white families. They tell black people to pull yourself up by your bootstraps; well, you stole our boots, and our shoestrings. But it first goes into our people, the leaders of Israel. Just as corrupt as Assyria was, we the Israelites were even more corrupt one towards another; that’s the reason the Lord sent Assyria against us.

“To turn aside the needy from judgment”: the needy are the Israelites, turned aside from true judgment and justice. “And to take away the right from the poor of my people”: the Israelites. America does this very same thing with unjust laws, but in cultural context our people were doing this while we were still in the land under Isaiah.

precepts.why: Always remember this and consider this in your studies, reading your four chapters every day. “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom”: God will show us the secrets of wisdom. “That they are double to that which is!”: many of the scriptures have dual meaning, double meaning. Although it may be talking about Assyria, or even our people at that time, it could also go for America at this time.

sense.text: “And in the desolation which shall come from far?”: the Lord said I’m going to bring destruction on you Israelites from far; he’s talking about Assyria coming. “To whom will ye flee for help?”: who are you going to run to? What you going to do when they come for you?

“Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners”: the Lord says without me you’re going to bow down under the prisoners. “For all this his anger is not turned away”: the Lord was very angry with us, very.
“O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger”: here the Lord was letting the Israelites know through Isaiah that Assyria was coming. Why? Because Israel, we was wicked as hell.

“I will send him against an hypocritical nation”: I will send Assyria against a hypocritical nation. Why does the Lord call us hypocritical? Because we had the word of God, we read the word of God, but we would not apply the word of God. This is what Deacon Malachi was talking about today in class, especially when it comes to marriage: we have the scriptures, do this, don’t do that, and people do what the Bible says don’t do. That’s a hypocrite for you. Men and women have the Bible but will not do a doggone thing the Bible says. “And to tread them down like the mire of the streets”: God commanded Assyria to tread us down like the mud in the streets. That’s some heavy stuff right there.

precepts.why: This is what Assyria did to us in captivity; anybody that conquered did this: they would put hooks in the nose and in the lip, so you had a lot of people with ripped lips and ripped noses. This is what the Lord says he’s going to do to the Assyrians because of what they did. “Therefore will I put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips”: why? Because that’s what Assyria was doing to us.

O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger. “Deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”: the Lord uses wicked nations to come against us; he uses these nations like a sword. During the time of Isaiah 10 he’s talking about Assyria being that rod of correction for us; in this day and age it’s America, it’s the so-called white man. “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

“Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men”. “Neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows”: that’s you young boys whose fathers died, or the women whose husbands died. “For every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer”: he’s talking about our people the Israelites. “And every mouth speaketh folly”: that word folly translates villainy.

sense.text: “Howbeit he meaneth not so”: God chose the Assyrian kings to come against our people for judgment, to correct us so we could get back in line with God’s word, just like he’s doing with us here in America. But Assyria didn’t understand that God was using them as a whipping stick against us. “Neither doth his heart think so”: he doesn’t think God is using him. “But it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.”
“Are not my princes altogether kings?”: this is what Assyria is saying.

“Is not Calno as Carchemish?”: he’s comparing the cities his predecessors had conquered with new cities, saying I’m going to take these cities too. “Is not Samaria as Damascus?”: he already had Damascus; now he says Samaria is just like that, I’ma take it too.

“As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, and whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria”: we had graven images throughout the land. That’s why in the books of Kings and Chronicles you read about the righteous kings tearing down the groves and tearing down the idols.

“Shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?”: verse 11 verifies that by this time Samaria was already conquered by Assyria. Now the campaign was against Judah, Jerusalem, the southern kingdom: Judah, Benjamin and a remnant of the Levites.

precepts.why: Idolatry is more than having an image set up that you’re worshipping; it goes much deeper than that. Everybody in here says they don’t worship idols, but watch what the prophet Ezekiel reveals. “These men have set up their idols in their heart”: meaning in their minds; they have idolatry in the mind. “Should I be enquired of at all by them?”: should I be questioned by these type of men? “I the Lord will answer him that cometh according to the multitude of his idols”. You may think you don’t worship idols, but if you put anything ahead of the word of the Most High, that’s idolatry: a wife, a spouse, your job, a car, sex, children. “Because they are all estranged from me through their idols.”

About covetousness, which is idolatry: money; some of you worship money, that’s your god. “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth”: mortify meaning dead in these things. “Evil concupiscence”: evil sexual thoughts. “And covetousness, which is idolatry”: any form of covetousness is idolatry in the sight of God. Anything you desire above what the word of God says is idolatry; it could be virtually anything, but only you and the Lord know what your idol is in your heart.

This is the Samaritan woman. “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”: 70 AD was coming. Christ was prophesying that the Romans were coming to destroy the land of Israel, so you wouldn’t be worshipping in the mountain where the Samaritans worshipped or in Jerusalem. “For salvation is of the Jews”: it means salvation is coming from Judah. Christ was from what tribe? Never forget that thing.

To prove that salvation is of Judah. “In Judah is God known”: that’s talking about Christ. This is what Christ was telling the Samaritan woman, because there was that split; Ephraim and them didn’t deal with the southern kingdom. Christ said, listen, salvation is of the Jews; if you want the kingdom, you got to come this way.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” “I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ”. “I that speak unto thee am he”: I am the Messiah, I’m the one that’s going to give salvation.

Here’s the mountain. When we came out of the wilderness, half of Israel stood upon one mountain to give the blessing and another group went on the other mountain to give the curse. “That thou shalt put the blessing upon mount Gerizim”: that’s the mountain the Samaritan woman was standing in and making reference to. “And the curse upon mount Ebal.”

sense.text: “When the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion”: his whole work means Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68, when he has destroyed Israel. “I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks”: when I finish with Jerusalem and Israel, I’ma deal with Assyria.

precepts.why: Here’s a precept. “For, lo, I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name”: that’s Jerusalem. “And should ye be utterly unpunished?”: should you other nations be utterly unpunished? I’m punishing my own people, and you think you’re going to get away? “For I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth”: I’m going to bring judgment on all nations on the earth. This verse is heavy, because many times on the street people try to give Europeans a pass for slavery. Did not the righteous Israelites go into slavery? Daniel, Ezekiel, Mordecai, Jeremiah, Habakkuk, and the three, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah: they all went into slavery. So if the righteous Israelites and all Israelites went into slavery, why do Europeans get a pass? All the righteous men and women in Israel went into slavery, but Caucasians get a pass? No, brothers; no, sisters. Nobody gets a pass.
